answer.text: Disclose in DD + ensure fair-treatment terms

explanation.text: The Logic: A co-investment service involves a PM offering its clients the opportunity to invest alongside the PM (or alongside another vehicle the PM manages). Because this creates potential for preferential treatment of one client cohort over another, regulatory and fiduciary principles require the PM to disclose the arrangement in the Disclosure Document and structure terms so that clients are treated fairly across the co-investment. The Trap: "Not disclose terms" directly contradicts the fiduciary disclosure obligation. Restricting co-investment to foreign clients has no regulatory basis. "Not charge fees" is unrelated — fees are permitted if disclosed. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-B Portfolio Managers workbook (Sep 2025) references co-investment only as exceptions to minimum-investment, direct-onboarding, net-worth, renewal/withdrawal, and custodian rules, and addresses fair treatment as a general PM duty, but does not state a specific co-investment Disclosure-Document and fair-treatment-terms requirement on the cited pages. The framing above is general PMS fiduciary practice.
